name: graphify.js
summary: Plugin that generates graph representations of code relationships and structure
purpose: Extends the OpenCode system with graph visualization capabilities, enabling developers to understand codebase topology, dependencies, and module relationships by transforming source metadata into navigable graph structures
responsibilities: Implement the OpenCode plugin contract via the GraphifyPlugin class
Access and resolve file system paths using Node.js fs and path modules
Parse and transform code relationships into graph data structures
Expose generated graph data for frontend visualization consumption
inputs: File system paths and source code locations
Plugin configuration and graph generation options
outputs: Structured graph data representing code relationships
architecture_notes: Operates as a plugin within the OpenCode extensibility layer, utilizing Node.js core modules (fs, path) to bridge static analysis with frontend visualization. The architecture suggests a build-time or hybrid runtime pattern where the plugin reads source topology and emits graph structures consumed by a frontend renderer. Located in a hidden .opencode/plugins directory, indicating internal infrastructure rather than userland extensions. The class-based design follows a standard plugin factory pattern.
improvements: Introduce an abstraction layer for file system operations to enable unit testing without mocking Node.js core modules
Add schema validation for generated graph data to ensure frontend contract compatibility
Implement streaming or incremental graph generation to handle large codebases efficiently
Add structured logging and error boundaries around file system access
Consider TypeScript interfaces to formalize the plugin contract and graph data types
